title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 15
statement: The figure is constructed from \(11\) line segments, each of which has length \(2.\) The area of pentagon \(ABCDE\) can be written as \(\sqrt m+\sqrt n,\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.text:
The right interior point is distance \(2\) from \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C,\) so these three points lie on a circle of radius \(2.\) Chords \(AB\) and \(BC\) also have length \(2,\) so each subtends \(60^\circ\) at the center. Thus \(AC=2\sqrt3.\) Similarly, the other half is its mirror image.

Put \(C=(-1,0),\) \(D=(1,0),\) and \(A=(0,\sqrt{11});\) then \(AC=AD=2\sqrt3.\) The other intersection of the radius-\(2\) circles centered at \(A\) and \(C\) is \[ B=\left(-\tfrac12-\tfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2\sqrt3}, \tfrac{\sqrt{11}}2+\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}\right), \] and \(E\) is its reflection across the \(y\)-axis.

Applying the shoelace formula to \(A,B,C,D,E\) gives \([ABCDE]=\sqrt{11}+2\sqrt3,\) which equals \(\sqrt{11}+\sqrt{12}.\)

So \(m+n=11+12=23.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Each interior point is distance \(2\) from three consecutive outer vertices, so it is their circumcenter
Since chords \(AB\) and \(BC\) have length equal to the radius \(2,\) \(AC=2\sqrt3;\) then use symmetric coordinates
